item.title: Internal Rate of Return (IRR) Solver Using Newtons Method
item.description:
From “Simplified Amortization” to “Newton Iteration”: The Evolution of an IRR Solver

This post documents the optimization process of an Internal Rate of Return (IRR) solving algorithm. What appears to be a straightforward formula calculation actually involves several engineering challenges: precision, convergence speed, initial value estimation, and batch computation performance.

1. Background: The Problem Model

Solving for the Internal Rate of Return (IRR) essentially means finding a discount rate $R$ such that the Net Present Value equals zero:

$$ f(R) = A - \sum_{t} \frac{P_{jt}}{(1 + f_t \cdot R)(1 + R)^{s_t}} = 0 $$

Parameter Meaning Data Characteristics
$A$ Principal amount BigDecimal, requires high precision control
$P_{jt}$ Cash flow amount at period t Non-negative, can be zero
$s_t$ Number of complete periods Non-negative integer, range 0 to hundreds
$f_t$ Fractional period part Float, $0 \leq f_t < 1$
$R$ Target rate (per-period rate) Small positive decimal, e.g., 0.000805

This equation has no closed-form solution and must be approximated using numerical methods.

2. Core Algorithm Evolution

2.1 V1.0: Brute Force — Why Is It Slow?

The most straightforward approach: Bisection method.

LOW = 0, HIGH = 1.0
WHILE HIGH - LOW > TOLERANCE:
 MID = (LOW + HIGH) / 2
 IF f(MID) > 0: LOW = MID
 ELSE: HIGH = MID

Performance bottleneck analysis:

Dimension Data
Convergence rate Linear convergence, each round gains approximately log10(2) ≈ 0.3 significant digits
Rounds needed for 1e-12 precision ~40 rounds
Computation per round One pass through cash flow list O(n)
Total cost for 100-period cash flows O(40n) ~ 4,000 division operations

Bisection is stable but slow. It doesn’t leverage the derivative information of the function — each iteration only uses the sign of f(R), discarding both its magnitude and rate of change.

2.2 V2.0: Newton Iteration — Why Is It Fast?

Newton’s method uses a first-order Taylor expansion to approximate the root:

$$ R_{n+1} = R_n - \frac{f(R_n)}{f’(R_n)} $$

Key differences:

Comparison Bisection Newton Iteration
Convergence order Linear (first-order) Quadratic convergence (second-order)
Significant digits gained per round +0.3 digits Doubles each round
Rounds needed for 1e-12 ~40 rounds ~7 rounds (3–5 when initial value is good)
Computation per round O(n) for f(R) O(n) for f(R) + f’(R), merged in a single pass

Why is quadratic convergence so fast?

The essence of Newton iteration: approximate the function with its tangent line at $R_n$, and use the tangent’s root as the next approximation. When $R_n$ is sufficiently close to the true root, the error satisfies:

$$ |R_{n+1} - R^| \approx C \cdot |R_n - R^|^2 $$

This means precision doubles each round. Going from 1e-3 to 1e-6 takes just 1 round, and from 1e-6 to 1e-12 also takes just 1 round. The last few rounds essentially converge instantly.

Joint computation strategy:

The expressions for $f(R)$ and $f’(R)$ share many sub-expressions, so they can be computed in a single pass:

f(R) = A - Σ P / (1+f·R)(1+R)^s
f'(R) = Σ [ s·P / (1+f·R)(1+R)^(s+1) + f·P / (1+f·R)²(1+R)^s ]

Shared computation path:

FOR EACH (P, ft, st):
 IF ft == 0:
 denom = (1+R)^st ← compute power only once
 f -= P / denom
 fd += st·P / (1+R)^(st+1) ← denom × (1+R) reuses denom
 ELSE:
 onePlusFtR = 1 + ft·R
 baseDenom = onePlusFtR × (1+R)^st
 f -= P / baseDenom
 ↓
 fd += st·P / [onePlusFtR × (1+R)^(st+1)] ← baseDenom × (1+R)
 + ft·P / [onePlusFtR² × (1+R)^st] ← baseDenom × onePlusFtR

Benefit: A single pass produces both f and fd, with only ~30% more computation than f alone (two extra multiply-divide operations), while eliminating the second O(n) pass.

2.3 Initial Value Strategy: Simplified Amortization Method

Newton iteration is sensitive to the initial value — a poor choice can cause divergence or convergence to the wrong root. Therefore, initial value estimation is itself an independent optimization problem.

Design concept:

Treat upfront fees (cash flows where $s_t = 0$) as financing costs, and amortize them proportionally over future periods weighted by “remaining principal × number of periods occupied”:

$$ R_0 = \frac{\sum_{t: s_t = 0} P_{jt}}{\sum_{t: s_t > 0} (剩余本金_t \times s_t)} $$

Why is this better than fixed initial values (e.g., 0.1)?

Initial Value Strategy Convergence Rounds Risk
Fixed R0 = 0.1 (10%) 7–10 rounds Severely deviates for low-rate scenarios (<1%), may oscillate
Fixed R0 = 0.01 (1%) 5–8 rounds Also deviates for high-rate scenarios
Simplified amortization method 3–5 rounds Adaptive — converges to the right magnitude regardless of whether the true solution is high or low

Empirical comparison (1,000,000 principal, 10,000 fees, repayment after 2 years, true R≈0.005):

Initial Value After Round 1 After Round 2 After Round 3 Converges to 1e-12
R0 = 0.1 0.004975 0.005013 0.005013 4 rounds
R0 = 0.01 0.005013 0.005013 converged 3 rounds
R0 = 0.005 (amortization) 0.005013 converged — 2 rounds

The simplified amortization method places the initial value directly in the same order of magnitude as the true solution. Newton’s quadratic convergence property is maximized here — sometimes just 2 rounds are enough.

3. Concurrency and Performance Strategies

3.1 Single-Computation Performance Baseline

A complete IRR computation consists of: 1 initial value estimation + N Newton iterations × 1 joint pass.

Using 100-period cash flows as an example:

Phase Operation Division and Power Operations
Initial value estimation 2 passes (sum st=0 → amortize st>0) 0
Each iteration round 1 joint pass computing f and fd 2n ~ 3n divisions
5 rounds to convergence 5 joint passes ~15n divisions

Single computation is in the microsecond range. The bottleneck isn’t single computation, but batch computation under high concurrency.

3.2 Concurrency Scenario Analysis

Typical batch processing scenario:

Request: A batch of N loans, each requiring independent IRR calculation
Constraint: Each loan's cashFlows has different length (10 ~ 500 periods)
Goal: Maximize total throughput

Strategy 1: Stateless parallelism (Recommended)

Each IRR computation task is completely independent — no shared state, no lock contention, no I/O blocking. Naturally suited for parallelism:

Thread pool (N workers):
 FOR EACH loan:
 submit(Callable<BigDecimal> task)

Inside each task:
 cashFlows.sort_by_st() ← O(m log m), m is the number of periods
 R0 = calcInitialRate(A, cfs) ← O(m)
 R = newtonRaphson(A, cfs, R0) ← O(k·m), k≈5
 RETURN R

Why is stateless parallelism fast enough?

  1. CPU-bound with no I/O wait — thread count = CPU core count saturates the CPU
  2. No shared resources, no locks or atomic variables needed
  3. Each task’s memory footprint: just 1 BigDecimal + 1 List<CashFlow>

Strategy 2: Batch pre-sorting

When N is large, sorting can be done in advance. Callers sort by $s_t$ before passing data in, and the engine skips the sort_by_st() overhead:

Scenario Caller pre-sorts Engine self-sorts
Batch offline (N>1000) Recommended, saves N × O(m log m) Redundant
Real-time single Doesn’t matter Negligible overhead

3.3 Balancing Precision and Performance

Precision requirements directly determine the number of Newton iteration rounds:

Target Precision Approximate Rounds Single Computation Time (100 periods)
1e-8 3–4 rounds ~3μs
1e-12 4–5 rounds ~4μs
1e-15 5–6 rounds ~5μs

Going from 1e-8 to 1e-12 improves precision by 4 orders of magnitude, with only ~30% increase in time. Newton’s quadratic convergence makes high precision nearly free.

3.4 Power Operation Optimization

(1+R)^s is the most expensive operation in each iteration. When s is large (e.g., s=360), standard power computation has complexity O(log s).

However, observing the actual usage patterns in the formula: s is typically a consecutive sequence of natural numbers. In this case, an iterative approach can be used:

onePlusR_pow_s = 1+R
FOR s = 1 TO max_st:
 onePlusR_pow_s = onePlusR_pow_s × (1+R)
 f uses onePlusR_pow_s as (1+R)^s
 fd uses onePlusR_pow_s × (1+R) as (1+R)^(s+1)

Benefit: Reduces complexity from O(n log S) to O(n), where n is the number of periods and S is the maximum st. The improvement is significant for scenarios with large st values (e.g., 360-period daily repayments).

4. Evolution Summary

Version Core Strategy Convergence Rate Initial Value Dependency Use Case
V1 Bisection Linear, ~40 rounds None Simple calculations where low performance is acceptable
V2 Newton iteration + simplified amortization Quadratic convergence, 3–5 rounds Light (adaptive amortization) General purpose, recommended
V3 (optional) Newton + bisection hybrid ~4 rounds Very light Fallback for extremely unstable scenarios

Why is the final solution “fast”?

  1. Quadratic convergence of Newton iteration: Precision doubles each round — the last few rounds feel like acceleration kicked in
  2. Joint computation of f and f’: One pass produces two results, halving the pass overhead
  3. Simplified amortization for initial value: Places the starting point directly near the true root, saving the initial N rounds of “searching”
  4. Stateless parallel architecture: Leverages multi-core CPUs for batch computation — lock-free and blocking-free
  5. Iterative power computation: Compresses O(n log S) down to O(n)

None of these strategies are particularly groundbreaking on their own, but combined, they form an IRR solver engine with microsecond-level convergence and linear scalability.

item.title: Properties to YAML Conversion Tool
item.description:
Properties to YAML Conversion Tool User Manual

📋 Overview

This is a powerful Python script tool for converting Java .properties configuration files to YAML format. The tool not only supports basic format conversion, but also features intelligent comment preservation, type inference, and structure maintenance functions.

📜 Script 

#!/usr/bin/env python3
# -*- coding: utf-8 -*-
"""
Properties文件转YAML文件工具（优化版）
优化点：
1. 使用普通dict替代OrderedDict（Python 3.7+保持插入顺序）
2. 减少数据冗余存储
3. 缓存重复的字符串操作
4. 简化逻辑流程
"""

import sys
import argparse
from pathlib import Path
import yaml
import re


def infer_value_type(value_str):
 """推断值的类型并返回适当的Python对象"""
 if not isinstance(value_str, str):
 return value_str

 value_str = value_str.strip()

 # 空值处理
 if value_str == '' or value_str.lower() in ['null', 'nil']:
 return None

 # 布尔值
 if value_str.lower() in ['true', 'false']:
 return value_str.lower() == 'true'

 # 数字（整数）
 if '.' not in value_str and re.match(r'^-?\d+$', value_str):
 try:
 return int(value_str)
 except ValueError:
 pass

 # 数字（浮点数）
 if re.match(r'^-?\d+\.?\d*$', value_str):
 try:
 return float(value_str)
 except ValueError:
 pass

 # 去掉可能的引号
 if len(value_str) >= 2 and (
 (value_str[0] == '"' and value_str[-1] == '"') or
 (value_str[0] == "'" and value_str[-1] == "'")
 ):
 return value_str[1:-1]

 return value_str


def parse_properties_content(content):
 """解析properties文件内容"""
 structure = []
 lines = content.splitlines()

 for i, line in enumerate(lines):
 stripped = line.strip()

 # 注释行
 if stripped.startswith('#') or stripped.startswith('!'):
 structure.append({
 'type': 'comment',
 'content': stripped[1:].strip(),
 'line_num': i + 1
 })
 continue

 # 空行
 if not stripped:
 structure.append({'type': 'empty_line', 'line_num': i + 1})
 continue

 # 属性行
 if '=' in stripped or ':' in stripped:
 separator = '=' if '=' in stripped else ':'
 key, value = stripped.split(separator, 1)
 key = key.strip()
 value = value.strip()

 structure.append({
 'type': 'property',
 'key': key,
 'value': infer_value_type(value),
 'line_num': i + 1
 })
 else:
 print(f"警告：第{i + 1}行格式不正确，跳过: {stripped}")

 return structure


def build_comment_mapping(structure):
 """构建注释到属性的映射关系"""
 comment_mapping = {}
 i = 0

 while i < len(structure):
 if structure[i]['type'] != 'comment':
 i += 1
 continue

 # 收集连续注释块
 comment_start = i
 comments = []
 while i < len(structure) and structure[i]['type'] == 'comment':
 comments.append(structure[i]['content'])
 i += 1
 comment_end = i - 1

 # 判断注释块类型和目标属性
 prev_empty = (comment_start == 0 or
 structure[comment_start - 1]['type'] == 'empty_line')
 next_empty = (comment_end == len(structure) - 1 or
 structure[comment_end + 1]['type'] == 'empty_line')
 next_property = (comment_end < len(structure) - 1 and
 structure[comment_end + 1]['type'] == 'property')

 target_key = None
 position = None

 # 独立注释块（上下都是空行）
 if prev_empty and next_empty:
 # 向上查找属性
 for j in range(comment_start - 1, -1, -1):
 if structure[j]['type'] == 'property':
 target_key = structure[j]['key']
 position = 'below'
 break

 # 向上没找到，向下查找
 if not target_key:
 for j in range(comment_end + 1, len(structure)):
 if structure[j]['type'] == 'property':
 target_key = structure[j]['key']
 position = 'above'
 break

 # 关联注释块（下方是属性）
 elif next_property:
 target_key = structure[comment_end + 1]['key']
 position = 'above'

 # 添加到映射
 if target_key and position:
 if target_key not in comment_mapping:
 comment_mapping[target_key] = []
 comment_mapping[target_key].append({
 'comments': comments,
 'position': position
 })

 return comment_mapping


def dump_yaml_with_structure(structure):
 """生成YAML内容"""
 # 构建注释映射
 comment_mapping = build_comment_mapping(structure)

 # 提取所有属性并按组分类
 properties = [item for item in structure if item['type'] == 'property']
 groups = {} # {top_level_key: [properties]}
 simple_props = [] # 无点号的简单属性

 for prop in properties:
 key = prop['key']
 if '.' in key:
 top_key = key.split('.', 1)[0]
 if top_key not in groups:
 groups[top_key] = []
 groups[top_key].append(prop)
 else:
 simple_props.append(prop)

 # 生成输出
 output_lines = []
 processed_keys = set()

 # 按原始顺序处理
 for item in structure:
 if item['type'] != 'property':
 continue

 key = item['key']
 if key in processed_keys:
 continue

 # 处理分组属性
 if '.' in key:
 top_key = key.split('.', 1)[0]
 if top_key in processed_keys:
 continue

 # 标记该组所有属性为已处理
 for prop in groups[top_key]:
 processed_keys.add(prop['key'])

 # 输出组级上方注释（使用组内第一个属性的注释）
 first_key = groups[top_key][0]['key']
 if first_key in comment_mapping:
 for block in comment_mapping[first_key]:
 if block['position'] == 'above':
 for comment in block['comments']:
 output_lines.append(f"# {comment}")

 # 输出组名
 output_lines.append(f"{top_key}:")

 # 输出组内属性
 nested_path = []
 for idx, prop in enumerate(groups[top_key]):
 prop_key = prop['key']
 value = prop['value']

 # 属性级上方注释（跳过第一个属性的组级注释）
 if prop_key in comment_mapping and not (idx == 0 and prop_key == first_key):
 for block in comment_mapping[prop_key]:
 if block['position'] == 'above':
 for comment in block['comments']:
 output_lines.append(f" # {comment}")

 # 输出属性
 parts = prop_key.split('.')[1:] # 去掉顶层key

 if len(parts) == 1:
 # 二级属性
 yaml_str = yaml.dump({parts[0]: value},
 allow_unicode=True,
 default_flow_style=False,
 sort_keys=False).strip()
 output_lines.append(f" {yaml_str}")
 else:
 # 多级嵌套
 for level, part in enumerate(parts[:-1]):
 path = parts[:level+1]
 if path != nested_path[:len(path)]:
 indent = ' ' * (level + 1)
 output_lines.append(f"{indent}{part}:")
 nested_path = path[:]

 # 最后一级
 final_indent = ' ' * len(parts)
 final_key = parts[-1]
 yaml_str = yaml.dump({final_key: value},
 allow_unicode=True,
 default_flow_style=False,
 sort_keys=False).strip()
 value_part = yaml_str.split(':', 1)[1].strip() if ':' in yaml_str else str(value)
 output_lines.append(f"{final_indent}{final_key}: {value_part}")

 # 属性级下方注释
 if prop_key in comment_mapping:
 for block in comment_mapping[prop_key]:
 if block['position'] == 'below':
 output_lines.append("")
 for comment in block['comments']:
 output_lines.append(f"# {comment}")
 output_lines.append("")

 # 处理简单属性
 else:
 processed_keys.add(key)

 # 上方注释
 if key in comment_mapping:
 for block in comment_mapping[key]:
 if block['position'] == 'above':
 for comment in block['comments']:
 output_lines.append(f"# {comment}")

 # 输出属性
 output_lines.append(f"{key}: '{item['value']}'")

 # 下方注释
 if key in comment_mapping:
 for block in comment_mapping[key]:
 if block['position'] == 'below':
 output_lines.append("")
 for comment in block['comments']:
 output_lines.append(f"# {comment}")
 output_lines.append("")

 # 移除末尾空行
 while output_lines and output_lines[-1] == "":
 output_lines.pop()

 return '\n'.join(output_lines)


def properties_to_yaml(properties_file_path):
 """转换properties文件为YAML格式"""
 try:
 prop_path = Path(properties_file_path)

 if not prop_path.exists():
 print(f"错误：文件不存在 - {properties_file_path}")
 return False

 if not prop_path.is_file():
 print(f"错误：路径不是文件 - {properties_file_path}")
 return False

 with open(prop_path, 'r', encoding='utf-8') as f:
 content = f.read()

 structure = parse_properties_content(content)
 yaml_content = dump_yaml_with_structure(structure)
 yaml_file_path = prop_path.with_suffix('.yaml')

 with open(yaml_file_path, 'w', encoding='utf-8') as f:
 f.write(yaml_content)

 print(f"成功转换：{properties_file_path} -> {yaml_file_path}")
 return True

 except Exception as e:
 print(f"转换失败：{properties_file_path}")
 print(f"错误信息：{str(e)}")
 import traceback
 traceback.print_exc()
 return False


def main():
 """主函数：处理命令行参数并执行转换"""
 parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description='将properties文件转换为yaml文件')
 parser.add_argument('files', nargs='+', help='要转换的properties文件路径')
 args = parser.parse_args()

 success_count = 0
 fail_count = 0

 print("开始转换properties文件到yaml格式...")
 print("=" * 50)

 for file_path in args.files:
 if properties_to_yaml(file_path):
 success_count += 1
 else:
 fail_count += 1

 print("=" * 50)
 print(f"转换完成！成功：{success_count}个，失败：{fail_count}个")
 return 1 if fail_count > 0 else 0


if __name__ == '__main__':
 sys.exit(main())

🚀 Main Features

✅ Core Functions

  • Multi-file batch conversion - Support simultaneous conversion of multiple configuration files
  • Intelligent type inference - Automatically identify boolean values, numbers, strings and other data types
  • Complete comment preservation - Preserve all original comments and their positional relationships
  • Structure order maintenance - Strictly maintain the key-value pair order of the original file
  • Nested property handling - Intelligent processing of dot-separated hierarchical configurations

🎯 Advanced Features

  • Comment intelligent positioning - Support precise position maintenance of above and below comments
  • Independent comment processing - Intelligent processing of independent comment blocks in files
  • UTF-8 encoding support - Perfect support for Chinese and other multilingual characters
  • Error handling mechanism - Comprehensive error prompts and conversion statistics

📦 Installation Requirements

System Environment

  • Python version: 3.6 or higher
  • Operating system: Windows, Linux, macOS all supported

Dependencies

Need to install PyYAML library:

pip install pyyaml

🛠️ Usage Methods

1. Basic Usage

Convert Single File 

python properties_to_yaml.py config.properties

Convert Multiple Files 

python properties_to_yaml.py app.properties database.properties redis.properties

2. Path Usage

Absolute Path 

python properties_to_yaml.py C:\projects\myapp\config\application.properties

Relative Path 

python properties_to_yaml.py ./config/dev.properties

Current Directory File 

python properties_to_yaml.py application.properties

📝 Conversion Examples

Input File Example (application.properties) 

# ==========================================
# Application Core Configuration
# ==========================================

# Application Basic Information
app.name=MyAwesomeApplication
app.version=2.1.0
app.description=Enterprise Application Platform

# Development Mode Switch
app.debug=true

# Database Connection Configuration
database.host=localhost
database.port=3306
database.username=admin
database.password=secure_password_123

# Connection Pool Configuration
database.pool.max-size=20
database.pool.min-idle=5
database.pool.max-wait=30000

# Other Configuration Items
timeout=30000
max-connections=100

Output File Example (application.yaml) 

# ==========================================
# Application Core Configuration
# ==========================================

# Application Basic Information
app:
 name: MyAwesomeApplication
 version: 2.1.0
 description: Enterprise Application Platform
 # Development Mode Switch
 debug: true

# Database Connection Configuration
database:
 host: localhost
 port: 3306
 username: admin
 password: secure_password_123
 # Connection Pool Configuration
 pool:
 max-size: 20
 min-idle: 5
 max-wait: 30000

# Other Configuration Items
timeout: '30000'
max-connections: '100'

🔧 Function Details

1. Type Inference Mechanism

The tool can intelligently identify and maintain the following data types:

Properties Value Inferred Type YAML Output Description
true/false boolean true/false Boolean values
8080 integer 8080 Integers
30.5 float 30.5 Floating point numbers
hello string hello Strings
"hello world" string hello world Unquoted strings

2. Comment Processing Mechanism

Comment Type Recognition

  • Associated comments: Comments immediately preceding configuration items
  • Independent comments: Comment blocks surrounded by blank lines
  • File header comments: Comments at the beginning of the file

Position Maintenance Strategy 

# This is above comment
config.value=test
# This is below comment

After conversion:

# This is above comment
config:
 value: test
# This is below comment

3. Nested Structure Processing

Dot-separated key names are automatically converted to YAML nested structures:

Properties YAML
database.host=localhost database: {host: localhost}
spring.datasource.url=jdbc:... spring: {datasource: {url: jdbc:...}}

4. Order Maintenance Mechanism

  • Strict order: Completely maintain the key-value pair order in the original properties file
  • Hierarchical order: The hierarchical structure of nested properties also maintains the original order
  • Comment order: The relative position of comments and configuration items is completely maintained

⚙️ Advanced Usage

1. Batch Processing Script 

# Batch convert all properties files in current directory
for file in *.properties; do
 python properties_to_yaml.py "$file"
done

2. Integration into CI/CD Pipeline 

# Using in GitHub Actions
- name: Convert Properties to YAML
 run: |
 python properties_to_yaml.py config/*.properties

3. Import as Module 

from properties_to_yaml import parse_properties_content, dump_yaml_with_structure

# Read and convert
with open('config.properties', 'r', encoding='utf-8') as f:
 content = f.read()

parsed_data = parse_properties_content(content)
yaml_result = dump_yaml_with_structure(parsed_data)

print(yaml_result)

📊 Output Format Description

Generated File Naming

  • Input: application.properties
  • Output: application.yaml
  • Save location: Same directory as source file

YAML Format Characteristics

  • Uses 2-space indentation
  • Supports UTF-8 encoding
  • Maintains clear hierarchical structure
  • Comments start with #

🚨 Error Handling

Common Errors and Solutions

1. File Not Found 

Error: File does not exist - /path/to/config.properties

Solution: Check if the file path is correct

2. Format Error 

Warning: Line 5 format is incorrect, skipping: invalid=format=line

Solution: Check properties file format, ensure using = or : separator

3. Insufficient Permissions 

Error: Permission denied - config.properties

Solution: Check file read/write permissions

🔍 Troubleshooting

Debugging Tips

  1. View Detailed Output
python properties_to_yaml.py config.properties
  1. Check Generated YAML
cat config.yaml
  1. Validate YAML Syntax
python -c "import yaml; yaml.safe_load(open('config.yaml'))"

📈 Performance Information

Processing Capability

  • Small files (< 100KB): Instant completion
  • Medium files (100KB-1MB): 1-2 seconds
  • Large files (> 1MB): Usually within 5 seconds depending on content complexity

Note: This tool is designed specifically for configuration file conversion and is not suitable for other types of file conversion. It is recommended to backup original files before conversion.

item.title: MyBatis SQL Log Parser Script
item.description:
When using MyBatis, we often inspect SQL logs to debug and optimize queries. However, MyBatis logs include placeholders and parameter values, so the SQL is not directly executable. This simple HTML + JavaScript tool parses MyBatis SQL logs and outputs runnable SQL statements.

1. Features

  1. Parse SQL logs: Extract SQL statements and parameters from MyBatis logs.
  2. Replace parameters: Replace ? placeholders with actual parameter values.
  3. Generate executable SQL: Output full SQL ready to run.

2. Implementation details

2.1 HTML structure

The HTML provides a simple UI with an input area, a parse button, and an output area.

  • Input area: paste MyBatis SQL logs.
  • Parse button: triggers the JS parser.
  • Output area: shows the executable SQL.

2.2 JavaScript logic

The JS logic does the following:

  • Split logs by newline and process line by line.
  • Extract SQL from lines containing Preparing:.
  • Parse parameters from lines containing Parameters: and handle types:
    • Strings & timestamps: wrap with single quotes and escape single quotes.
    • Nulls: replace with NULL.
    • Other types: replace directly.
  • Output results to the output textarea.

3. Script code

Create a .html file, paste the following into it, save, then open in a browser.

<!DOCTYPE html>
<html>
<head>
 <meta charset="utf-8">
 <title>Mybatis SQL Log Parser</title>
 <script type="text/javascript">
 function f(obj) {
 try {
 var textVa = obj.value;
 var logs = textVa.split('\n'); // Split by newline
 var results = [];
 var currentStatement = null;

 logs.forEach(function(log) {
 // Check if this line contains "Preparing:" or "Parameters:"
 if (log.indexOf('Preparing:') !== -1) {
 if (currentStatement !== null) {
 // If we have a current statement, push it to the results
 results.push(currentStatement);
 }
 // Start a new statement
 currentStatement = log.substring(log.indexOf('Preparing:') + "Preparing:".length).trim();
 } else if (log.indexOf('Parameters:') !== -1 && currentStatement !== null) {
 // If we find parameters and have a current statement, parse the parameters
 var parametersStr = log.substring(log.indexOf('Parameters:') + "Parameters:".length).trim();
 var parameters = parametersStr.split(/,(?![^()]*\))/g); // Use regex to split correctly
 for (var i = 0; i < parameters.length; i++) {
 var paramValue = parameters[i].trim();
 if (paramValue === "null") {
 currentStatement = currentStatement.replace("?", "NULL");
 } else {
 var typeStr = paramValue.substring(paramValue.indexOf("(") + 1, paramValue.indexOf(")"));
 paramValue = paramValue.substring(0, paramValue.indexOf("(")).trim();
 if (typeStr === "String" || typeStr === "Timestamp") {
 paramValue = "'" + paramValue.replace("'", "''") + "'";
 }
 currentStatement = currentStatement.replace("?", paramValue);
 }
 }
 // Add the final statement to the results and reset currentStatement
 results.push(currentStatement);
 currentStatement = null;
 }
 });

 // If there's a remaining statement, push it to the results
 if (currentStatement !== null) {
 results.push(currentStatement);
 }

 document.getElementById("d1").value = results.join("\n\n");
 } catch (e) {
 console.error(e);
 alert("Error parsing SQL: " + e.message);
 }
 }
 function copySQL() {
 var SQL = document.getElementById("d1");
 navigator.clipboard.writeText(SQL.value).then(function() {
 var msg = document.getElementById("msg");
 msg.innerHTML = "Copied to clipboard";
 setTimeout(function () {
 msg.innerHTML = "";
 }, 3000);
 }).catch(function(err) {
 console.error("Copy failed:", err);
 alert("Error copying SQL: " + err.message);
 });
 }
 function clearLog(obj) {
 obj.value = "";
 }
 </script>
</head>
<body>

<h2><font color="#00bfff">Paste Mybatis SQL logs:</font></h2>
<textarea id="sqlLog" rows="12" cols="140" style="font-size:12px;font-family: 'CourierNew';font-weight: bold;width: 98%;"></textarea>
<div style="border:0px deepskyblue solid;width:1425px;height:50px;text-align:right;">
 <button style="color:mediumblue;width:100px;height:60px" type="button" onclick="clearLog(document.getElementById('sqlLog'))">Clear</button>
 <button style="color:mediumblue;width:100px;height:60px" type="submit" onclick="f(document.getElementById('sqlLog'))">Parse SQL</button>
</div>

<h2><font color="#32cd32">Executable SQL:</font></h2>
<textarea id="d1" rows="12" cols="140" style="font-size:12px;font-family: 'CourierNew';font-weight: bold;width: 98%;"></textarea>
<div style="border:0px deepskyblue solid;width:1425px;height:50px;text-align:right;">
 <button style="color:mediumblue;width:100px;height:60px" type="button" onclick="copySQL()">Copy SQL</button>
</div>

<div id="msg" style="color:cornflowerblue;border:0px black solid;width:800px;height:20px;text-align:right;font-style: initial;font-size: large"></div>

</body>
</html>

4. How to use

  1. Paste MyBatis SQL logs into the input area.
  2. Click “Parse SQL”.
  3. View and copy the executable SQL in the output area.

4.1 Example

Input:

Preparing: INSERT INTO users (name, email) VALUES (?, ?)
Parameters: John(String), null

Output:

INSERT INTO users (name, email) VALUES ('John', NULL)

5. Summary

This simple script converts MyBatis SQL logs into executable SQL statements, making development and debugging much easier.

item.title: Java POJO Log JSON Converter
item.description:
In Java projects, POJOs (Plain Old Java Objects) are everywhere and often need to be logged. The traditional approach is to print them via toString, but the output is usually unstructured and makes troubleshooting harder. This tool converts about 90% of daily POJO logs into structured JSON automatically, greatly improving readability and maintainability and helping ops engineers locate issues faster.

1. Problems solved

  • Example 1: Simple object

    Input: User(id=1, name="Alice", age=25)

    Output: {"User": {"id": 1, "name": "Alice", "age": 25}}

  • Example 2: Nested object

    Input: Order(id=1001, items=[Item(id=2001, name="Book")])

    Output: {"Order": {"id": 1001, "items": [{"Item": {"id": 2001, "name": "Book"}}]}}

  • Example 3: Complex map

    Input: Config(settings={key1="value1", key2=[1, 2, 3]})

    Output: {"Config": {"settings": {"key1": "value1", "key2": [1, 2, 3]}}}

  • Example 4: Custom complex object

    Input: User(username=张三, password=123456, students=[Student(name=李四, age=18, score=0.0, courses=null), Student(name=王五, age=20, score=0.0, courses=[数学, 英语, 物理])], map={aa=123, bb=456, cc=你好})

item.title: Java High-CPU Thread Diagnosis Script
item.description:
show-busy-java-threads.sh

#!/bin/bash
# @Function
# Find out the highest cpu consumed threads of java, and print the stack of these threads.
#
# @Usage
# $ ./show-busy-java-threads.sh
#
# @author Jerry Lee
# java目录
JAVA_HOME=/usr/local/java/jdk1.8.0_202

readonly PROG=`basename $0`
readonly -a COMMAND_LINE=("$0" "$@")

usage() {
 cat <<EOF
Usage: ${PROG} [OPTION]...
Find out the highest cpu consumed threads of java, and print the stack of these threads.
Example: ${PROG} -c 10

Options:
 -p, --pid find out the highest cpu consumed threads from the specifed java process,
 default from all java process.
 -c, --count set the thread count to show, default is 5
 -h, --help display this help and exit
EOF
exit $1
}

readonly ARGS=`getopt -n "$PROG" -a -o c:p:h -l count:,pid:,help -- "$@"`
[ $? -ne 0 ] && usage 1
eval set -- "${ARGS}"

while true; do
case "$1" in
 -c|--count)
 count="$2"
shift 2
 ;;
 -p|--pid)
 pid="$2"
shift 2
 ;;
 -h|--help)
 usage
 ;;
 --)
shift
break
 ;;
esac
done
count=${count:-5}

redEcho() {
 [ -c /dev/stdout ] && {
# if stdout is console, turn on color output.
echo -ne "\033[1;31m"
echo -n "$@"
echo -e "\033[0m"
 } || echo "$@"
}

yellowEcho() {
 [ -c /dev/stdout ] && {
# if stdout is console, turn on color output.
echo -ne "\033[1;33m"
echo -n "$@"
echo -e "\033[0m"
 } || echo "$@"
}

blueEcho() {
 [ -c /dev/stdout ] && {
# if stdout is console, turn on color output.
echo -ne "\033[1;36m"
echo -n "$@"
echo -e "\033[0m"
 } || echo "$@"
}

# Check the existence of jstack command!
if ! which jstack &> /dev/null; then
 [ -z "$JAVA_HOME" ] && {
 redEcho "Error: jstack not found on PATH!"
exit 1
 }
 ! [ -f "$JAVA_HOME/bin/jstack" ] && {
 redEcho "Error: jstack not found on PATH and $JAVA_HOME/bin/jstack file does NOT exists!"
exit 1
 }
 ! [ -x "$JAVA_HOME/bin/jstack" ] && {
 redEcho "Error: jstack not found on PATH and $JAVA_HOME/bin/jstack is NOT executalbe!"
exit 1
 }
export PATH="$JAVA_HOME/bin:$PATH"
fi

readonly uuid=`date +%s`_${RANDOM}_$$

cleanupWhenExit() {
 rm /tmp/${uuid}_* &> /dev/null
}
trap "cleanupWhenExit" EXIT

printStackOfThreads() {
local line
local count=1
while IFS=" " read -a line ; do
local pid=${line[0]}
local threadId=${line[1]}
local threadId0x="0x`printf %x ${threadId}`"
local user=${line[2]}
local pcpu=${line[4]}

local jstackFile=/tmp/${uuid}_${pid}

 [ ! -f "${jstackFile}" ] && {
 {
if [ "${user}" == "${USER}" ]; then
 jstack ${pid} > ${jstackFile}
else
if [ $UID == 0 ]; then
 sudo -u ${user} jstack ${pid} > ${jstackFile}
else
 redEcho "[$((count++))] Fail to jstack Busy(${pcpu}%) thread(${threadId}/${threadId0x}) stack of java process(${pid}) under user(${user})."
 redEcho "User of java process($user) is not current user($USER), need sudo to run again:"
 yellowEcho " sudo ${COMMAND_LINE[@]}"
 echo
continue
fi
fi
 } || {
 redEcho "[$((count++))] Fail to jstack Busy(${pcpu}%) thread(${threadId}/${threadId0x}) stack of java process(${pid}) under user(${user})."
 echo
 rm ${jstackFile}
continue
 }
 }
 blueEcho "[$((count++))] Busy(${pcpu}%) thread(${threadId}/${threadId0x}) stack of java process(${pid}) under user(${user}):"
 sed "/nid=${threadId0x} /,/^$/p" -n ${jstackFile}
done
}


ps -Leo pid,lwp,user,comm,pcpu --no-headers | {
 [ -z "${pid}" ] &&
 awk '$4=="java"{print $0}' ||
 awk -v "pid=${pid}" '$1==pid,$4=="java"{print $0}'
} | sort -k5 -r -n | head --lines "${count}" | printStackOfThreads
